issues.title: Failed/dropped USE KEYSPACE discards new connections and can permanently break the pool
issues.verdictReason: handle_ready_connection's new Err(ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace(err)) arm (line 900) drops the connection and, if the pool is empty, calls update_shared_conns(Some(err.into())) which sets shared_conns to Broken (line 1128-1130); emit_events (line 1158) turns a Ready->empty transition into ConnectivityChangeEvent::Lost. Before this PR, start_setting_keyspace_for_connection (then ~line 1319) always returned Ok((connection, error_receiver)) and only warn!-logged a failed USE, so the connection was kept. current_keyspace is set at line 1287 before USE is verified and is pre-existing, unchanged behavior, but combined with the new discard-on-failure logic it means a typo'd or dropped keyspace makes every refill fail USE, so the pool never recovers and the node is reported Lost/unreachable, whereas before it stayed usable for fully-qualified queries.
issues.scopeReason: The discard-on-keyspace-failure behavior is exactly what commit 7f48315d added.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: The refiller stores current_keyspace before knowing whether USE succeeded and never clears it, so a failed use_keyspace or a DROP KEYSPACE of the session's keyspace causes every new connection to be thrown away, draining pools that never refill, blocking newly discovered nodes from opening any connection, and causing HostListener to report the node as down via a spurious Lost event.
reportedAs.builtin-code-review: Every failed USE now discards the new connection instead of keeping it; since the keyspace comes from current_keyspace (set by use_keyspace at line 1287 before the request succeeds), a failed use_keyspace call or a keyspace dropped after USE leaves a name every later connection fails to set, so after a node restart every refill is discarded and retried with growing delays, leaving the pool permanently Broken(UseKeyspaceError).
reportedAs.ce-code-review: PoolRefiller::use_keyspace saves current_keyspace before knowing if USE succeeded; after a failed use_keyspace or a DROPped keyspace, every new connection fails USE, gets dropped, and refill is rescheduled endlessly, eventually leaving every node's pool Broken(UseKeyspaceError) and failing all requests to that node.
reportedAs.mattpocock-review: PoolRefiller::use_keyspace stores current_keyspace before the USE is checked and never reverts it on failure; after this PR, a nonexistent or dropped keyspace makes every refill connection fail, draining the pool to Broken(UseKeyspaceError) and causing emit_events to send ConnectivityChangeEvent::Lost, marking up nodes as down.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: use_keyspace sets current_keyspace before knowing whether USE succeeded and never rolls it back, so a failed USE now drops the connection instead of joining the pool with a warning as before; refill connections keep failing USE and the pool ends up Broken(UseKeyspaceError).
reportedAs.tob-diff-review: current_keyspace is set before USE is verified to succeed, so a keyspace typo or a later-dropped keyspace causes every new connection to be discarded with ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace and refill retried with growing backoff forever, leaving the pool permanently Broken(UseKeyspaceError) once existing connections die.
reportedAs.tob-rust-review: A failed USE now drops the new connection instead of adding it to the pool, and current_keyspace is set before USE runs and never cleared on failure, so one bad use_keyspace call or a dropped keyspace causes every refill to fail USE and drain the pool to empty, marking the node Broken/unreachable.

issues.title: Failed USE for a stale keyspace is discarded instead of retried with the current keyspace
issues.verdictReason: The Ok arm (line 915) re-checks evt.keyspace_name against self.current_keyspace and re-dispatches start_setting_keyspace_for_connection if the keyspace changed mid-flight, but the Err(ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace(err)) arm (line 900) does no such comparison - it always drops the connection and marks had_error_since_last_refill, even if current_keyspace has since moved on to a different (valid) keyspace.
issues.scopeReason: This asymmetry only exists because commit 7f48315d added the discard-on-keyspace-failure path; previously failures didn't discard, so there was nothing to retry.

reportedAs.ce-code-review: The error arm never compares evt.keyspace_name with current_keyspace (unlike the Ok arm), so if USE ks1 fails after the user already switched to ks2, the connection is thrown away and counted as an error instead of being retried with ks2.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: If the user switches keyspace while USE old_ks is running and it fails, the connection is thrown away and backoff grows, instead of being retried with the new keyspace.
reportedAs.tob-diff-review: If current_keyspace changes while an older USE is still in flight and that USE fails, the connection is dropped and marked as error rather than resent through start_setting_keyspace_for_connection with the new keyspace, unlike the success branch which already re-checks evt.keyspace_name against current_keyspace.

issues.title: Commit message "avoid busy-waiting" claim disputed as not matching the change
issues.verdictReason: Verified commit 617139df replaces tokio::task::yield_now().await with tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(1)).await inside the polling loop. yield_now() is a textbook busy-wait (immediately reschedulable, spins as fast as the executor allows); sleep(1ms) actually yields real wall-clock time between checks and meaningfully cuts CPU usage. The commit message accurately describes what the change does, even though the loop is still a poll rather than a fully event-driven wait.
issues.scopeReason: The commit and its message are part of this PR.

issues.verdictReason: Ran `cargo test -p scylla --lib --features metrics network::connection_pool` (8 passed, 1 failed) and again without --features metrics (5 passed, 1 failed); the sole failure both times is many_connections panicking with ConnectTimeout. Reproduced the identical panic on a clean `main` worktree (same file, same ConnectTimeout), confirming it is a pre-existing, environment-dependent failure (likely too many concurrent connection attempts / ephemeral-port pressure in this sandbox) unrelated to this PR's changes.
issues.scopeReason: Reproduced on main; not caused by this PR.

reportedAs.ce-code-review: The new tests pass with and without --features metrics and none are flaky; the one observed failure in that module (many_connections) needs a live node and is unrelated.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: Running cargo test -p scylla --lib --features metrics network::connection_pool gave 8 of 9 passing; the one failure, many_connections, needs a live Scylla node and fails the same way on main.

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-2026-09-29/quillstone/ce-code-r: New tests pass reliably with and without the metrics feature.
reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-2026-09-29/quillstone/superpowe: many_connections test fails, but same failure exists on main.

issues.title: decrement_total_connections/metrics test use a single-decrement loop and a polling sleep…
issues.verdictReason: Verified decrement_total_connections (line 1360) loops `for _ in 0..count { self.metrics.dec_total_connections(); }` instead of a single fetch_sub(count); a Metrics::sub_total_connections(n) helper would indeed be simpler, though functionally equivalent. Also verified full_pool_clears_excess_connections_and_balances_metrics (around line 1972) polls metrics.get_total_connections() in a 1ms-sleep loop under a 5s timeout rather than using a notification - functionally correct but not fully deterministic.
issues.scopeReason: Both are new code added by this PR.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: decrement_total_connections calls fetch_sub(1) once per connection; a Metrics::sub_total_connections(n) doing a single fetch_sub(n) would be simpler and update the counter in one step.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: decrement_total_connections calls dec_total_connections in a loop; a single decrement-by-N helper would be simpler. Also: the metrics test uses a 1 ms sleep loop inside a 5 s timeout; it isn't flaky, but paused time or a notification would make it deterministic.

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-2026-09-29/quillstone/anthropic: decrement_total_connections decrements one at a time instead of in bulk.
reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-2026-09-29/quillstone/superpowe: decrement_total_connections loops single decrements instead of a batch helper / Metrics test uses a polling sleep loop instead of a deterministic wait.
